# Final Touches — Murim Login

## Goal

Prepare one mastered chapter for readers. This pass adds footnotes, repairs formatting, and fixes duplicate or missing sentences. It is not a fluency rewrite.

Keep the mastered prose. Change a sentence only to attach a footnote, repair System / thought / speech / chat formatting, restore a source sentence the English dropped, or remove an English sentence the Korean does not support.

## Duplicates and omissions

Compare the English with the Korean source.

- Restore source facts, events, dialogue, and sentences the English dropped, in the same place in the scene.
- Remove English sentences that have no support in the Korean.
- Keep a bold label that names a quoted document, manual, warning, or sign, such as `> **Warning**`. Keep it when this chapter recalls or reprints a notice that was labeled earlier, even if the Korean reprint shows only the body.
- Keep repetition the Korean itself repeats: comedy, panic, emphasis, echoed dialogue, and short beats such as `……`.
- Do not treat a short refrain or a deliberate echo as a duplicate.

## Footnotes

Use Markdown footnotes (`[^1]`, `[^2]`, …). Number them in order of first appearance, starting at 1 for this chapter. Put every definition in one block at the end of the file.

Within this chapter, write one definition for a term, unit, amount, or reference. Every later occurrence of that same thing reuses the same marker. `goshiwon` five times is one note, and so is `hyung`. A different amount or a different term gets its own note. Another chapter may carry its own note for the same term.

Write notes in factual English. No spoilers and no jokes added by the note. Romanize words. A note may include the original character when it is explaining that character. Keep Hangul jamo already used as chat reactions, such as ㅋㅋ and ㄷㄷ.

Add a note only when an English reader would otherwise miss the meaning or the conversion. Skip it when the sentence already says what the reference means. A translated proverb whose warning is plain, a joke the next line completes, a place name used as a place, and a fictional law the dialogue already describes do not get notes.

Skip a conversion footnote when the prose already states both metric and imperial for that quantity.

### Won

Footnote Korean won, including round figures and vague amounts (“hundreds of millions of won”), when the prose does not already give the conversion. Use only the project rates in the packet. Show dollars, then euros, as approximate figures. Round large amounts to about two significant figures and say “about.” For a vague amount, give the approximate range those words cover. One note per distinct amount; reuse it for every later mention of that same amount.

Do not convert traditional money (nyang, taels, cash) or Chinese yuan with the won rate. Explain those with a cultural or historical note only when the English does not already carry the meaning.

### Units

Footnote a Korean or Chinese traditional unit, or a metric quantity, once in the chapter, with both metric and imperial, using this table:

| Unit | Use | Metric | Imperial |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pyeong (평) | area | 3.31 m² | 35.6 ft² |
| geun (근) | Korean weight | 600 g | 1.32 lb |
| ja / cheok (자) | length | 30.3 cm | 11.9 in |
| chi (치) | length | 3.03 cm | 1.19 in |
| don (돈) | weight | 3.75 g | 0.132 oz |
| gwan (관) | weight | 3.75 kg | 8.27 lb |
| ri (리), Korea | distance | 393 m | 0.244 mi |
| li (里), China | distance | 500 m | 0.311 mi |
| jin (斤), modern Chinese | weight | 500 g | 1.10 lb |
| liang (两), modern Chinese | weight | 50 g | 1.76 oz |

Choose Korean ri or Chinese li from the setting. Say which one the note uses.

Also footnote metric quantities already in the English (kilometers, meters, centimeters, kilograms, grams, liters, square meters, degrees Celsius) with the imperial equivalent. Use unit words or abbreviations (`ft`, `in`, `mi`, `lb`, `oz`, `gal`). Do not use `"` or `'` as unit marks.

### Cultural references

Footnote a Korean, Chinese, or other Asian word, custom, institution, food, joke, or allusion when the English does not already carry it: `goshiwon`, `hyung`, `doenjang`, `jeonse`. Explain it in one or two sentences. One note per term in the chapter, reused by every later occurrence.

Leave it unnoted when the English is already clear. Do not explain a proverb the translation has already stated, a pun the scene completes, or ordinary vocabulary.

Do not footnote standing series vocabulary. Never add a note whose job is to define any of these, including ordinary variants and compounds:

- Murim
- qi, including demonic qi, innate qi, and qi deviation
- dantian, including the Upper, Middle, and Lower Dantian
- internal energy
- mana

A note about something else may mention these words. Do not attach a marker to them.

## Formatting

Enforce these four patterns. Repair System, speech, thought, and chat formatting when it drifts. Leave every other blockquote heading as it stands.

- **System.** Each real game System panel is one Markdown blockquote headed exactly `> **System**`. Keep the panel’s lines inside that blockquote. Start a new panel only when prose intervenes. Keep every `> **System**` panel from the mastered chapter, including a notice the narrator only hears. Do not turn a panel into italics, a sound effect, or narration. Do not wrap System text in square brackets or label a manual, sign, or ordinary quotation as System. A manual or remembered notice keeps its own label, such as `> **Warning**` or `> **Product User Manual**`. That label is not a System panel, and it is not drift.
- **Speech.** Spoken dialogue uses curly double quotes (`“` `”`). Not straight quotes, not italics.
- **Thoughts.** Direct thoughts are italics with no quotation marks. Keep a mastered thought in italics. Do not turn it into spoken dialogue.
- **Chat and comments.** Public comment threads and private chat logs shown as threads are one blockquote. Each message line begins with `└`, as in `> └ **Name:** message`. Keep a thread title that is not itself a message, such as `> **Peace Guild**`, on its own line above the messages. Do not add a `**Chat**` heading. A status line that is only a name or level, such as `> **Lv. 22 Hyuk Mujin**`, is not a chat message. Leave that line unchanged, including the bold. Ordinary spoken dialogue stays in curly quotes.
- **Headings.** The only Markdown heading is `# Chapter N`. Do not add `##` or `###`. A diary title or similar label stays a bold line, `**Training Day 1**`, even when the mastered copy used a smaller heading.

Leave narration as narration. Scene breaks stay `* * *`, with the same count as the source.

## Output contract

Return only the complete English Markdown chapter. The first nonblank line must be `# Chapter N`. No status line and no model preamble. Do not add Hangul syllables. Chat jamo and a character cited in a note may stay.

## Project conversion rates

These rates are binding. Do not look up or substitute a market rate.

- 1 US dollar = 1400 Korean won
- 1 euro = 1550 Korean won

Convert every won amount with these rates. In each footnote, give dollars first and euros second.

동시에 확신이 들었다.

‘에어 브레스(Air Breath).’

용족에게만 허락된 고유 능력의 한 갈래.

쩌적, 그그극.

어깨를 짓누르는 압력을 견디며 묵묵히 나아갔다.

한 걸음, 한 걸음마다 발목이 지면에 파묻히고 압력이 힘을 더해 갔지만 내 발걸음을 막을 수 없었다.

놈이 일반적인 몬스터의 한계를 벗어난 존재라고 해도 두렵지 않다.

‘그건 나도 마찬가지니까.’

적어도 신체 능력에 한해서라면 나는 이미 초인(超人)이라 불려도 좋았다.

쿠웅-!

단 한 번의 발 구름과 함께 나는 화살처럼 쏘아졌다.

당황한 놈이 고개를 틀어 에어 브레스를 쏟아 냈지만 내 속도를 쫓아올 수는 없었다.

쉬쉭! 타다다닥!

가벼운 가죽 갑옷과 창 한 자루만을 들고 번개처럼 전장을 가로지른 나는 어느새 놈의 앞까지 다다라 있었다.

- 크르르륵?

당황한 놈이 접고 있던 날개를 활짝 폈다. 그러나 그때는 이미 내가 힘껏 도약한 후였다.

쾅!

강렬한 진동과 함께 나는 훨훨 날아올랐다. 바람에 흩날리는 머리카락 사이, 번쩍거리는 흑색 비늘에 뒤덮인 놈의 무릎이 보였다. 소위 십자인대라 불리는 바로 그 부위다.

“넌 군 면제다. 이 새끼야!”

외침과 함께 온 힘을 다해 창을 찔러 넣었다.

푹! 서걱!

어지간한 마법도, 무기도 통하지 않는다는 와이번의 가죽과 비늘이 단숨에 갈라진다.

작살로 물고기를 잡은 것처럼 찌릿한 손맛이 손끝을 타고 전해졌다.

‘들어갔다!’

푸르게 타오르는 창기는 막아서는 모든 것을 가르고 부쉈다.

쾅! 푸화아아악!

거무죽죽한 피가 분수처럼 솟구쳤다. 막 날개를 펴고 하늘로 날아오르려던 놈이 비명과 함께 무릎을 꿇었다.

- 그워어어어어!

하지만 나는 거기서 멈추지 않았다. 놈의 무릎에 박아넣은 창대의 끝부분을 밟고 그 탄력을 실어 몸을 튕겼다.

그렇게 다시 한번 수 미터를 솟구치는 내 손아귀엔 어느새 단검이 들려 있었다.

‘없으면 꺼내면 되지.’

무림뿐만 아니라 현실의 인벤토리에도 수많은 무기가 저장되어 있다.

일전에 거금을 들여 구입한 물건들이지만, 놈을 죽이기 위해서라면 그 열 배를 쏟아부어도 아깝지 않다.

푹!

문득 무림에서 벽호공(壁虎功)을 수련할 때가 생각났다. 그때 올랐던 절벽은 더욱 높았고 발을 디딜 만한 무언가도 마땅치 않았다.

‘어느 정도 올라왔다 싶으면 웬 미친놈이 바위도 떨어트리고 그랬지.’

그때에 비하면 그리 어려울 것도 없다.

나는 놈의 거대한 동체에 단검을 쉴 새 없이 박으며 위로, 더 위로 솟구쳤다.

푹, 푸푹! 푸푸푸푹!

창기 앞에서는 철갑보다 단단한 외피도, 하급 마법도 튕겨 낸다는 비늘도 아무런 소용이 없었다.

손바닥만 한 뭔가가 자신의 몸을 기어오르며 계속해서 대못을 박는다고 생각하면 쉽다. 지금의 놈이 바로 그랬다.

- 크와아아아악!

끊임없이 엄습하는 고통을 참지 못한 놈이 괴성과 함께 몸부림쳤다. 나를 떨쳐 내려는 시도였겠지만 한발 늦었다.

그때 난 이미 허공에서 부유감(浮游感)을 만끽하고 있었으니까.

‘인벤토리 오픈. 창 장착.’

다음 순간, 텅 비어 있던 손아귀에 단단한 창대가 잡혔다.

임독양맥을 타통하며 일 갑자를 넘어선 열양지기가 창날을 향해 썰물처럼 밀려든다.

쏴아아악. 츠츠츠!

창날을 빈틈없이 감싼 푸른색의 염화(炎火).

어둠 속에서 일렁이는 그것은 유성의 꼬리였고, 나는 유성 그 자체였다.

“어딜 도망치려고.”

나직한 중얼거림과 함께 창과 한 몸이 된 나는 빠르게 내리꽂혔다. 목표는 놈의 앞발이자 팔이라 할 수 있는 날개.

고통에 잠시 눈이 먼 놈에게는 유성을 막을 수 있는 방법이 존재하지 않았다.

화륵, 촤아아악!

작은 태양처럼 이글거리는 열양지기가 가죽과 비늘을 가르고 살을 태운다. 세로 직경만 10여 미터에 달하는 날개가 창날을 따라 반으로 쪼개졌다.

- 크륵……!

아마도 난생처음 겪어 본 극통일 것이다. 일평생 포식자로만 살았던 놈의 붉은 눈동자가 부릅떠졌다.

- 크와아아아아아악!

사뿐하게 지면에 착지한 나는 가라앉은 눈빛으로 놈을 응시했다.

뿌옇게 피어오른 흙먼지 속에서 50m의 거체가 몸부림치고 있었다.

“아프냐?”

- 크왁! 크아아아!

“겨우 그 정도로?”

3년 전, 놈이 했던 것에 비하면 이건 아무것도 아니다.

날갯짓 한 번에 전신이 박살 났고, 발톱으로 움켜쥔 머리통은 흔적도 없이 사라졌다. 거대한 아가리에 삼켜진 이들은 시체조차 찾지 못했다.

그때 처음으로 알았다.

인간의 몸에 이토록 많은 피와 장기가 있다는 것을. 이렇게 잔인하게 죽을 수도 있다는 것을.

A spearhead wreathed in blue flames filled his enormous eye.

Crunch!

Crunch!

They had cost me a fortune, but if it meant killing this creature, I wouldn’t mind spending ten times as much.

Thrust!

I suddenly remembered training in the Wall Lizard Technique back in Murim. The cliff I had scaled then was even higher, and there had hardly been anything to use as a foothold.

*And whenever I thought I’d made some progress, a certain lunatic would start dropping rocks on me.*

Compared to that, this was nothing.

I drove my dagger into the creature’s enormous body again and again, climbing higher and higher.

Thrust, thrust! Thrust-thrust-thrust!

Against Spear Energy, neither hide harder than plate armor nor scales capable of deflecting low-level magic were of any use.

Imagine something the size of your palm crawling up your body and hammering nails into you over and over.

That was exactly what the creature was going through.

—Kraaaaaaah!

Unable to endure the relentless pain, it writhed and roared. It was trying to shake me off, but it was one step too late.

By then, I was already savoring the sensation of floating through the air.

*Open Inventory. Equip spear.*

The next instant, a solid spear shaft filled my empty hand.

The Scorching Yang Qi that had surpassed one jiazi when I opened my Conception and Governor Vessels surged toward the spearhead like an ebbing tide.[^6]

Whoooooosh. Ssssss!

Blue flames enveloped the spearhead without leaving the slightest gap.

Flickering in the darkness, they were the tail of a meteor.

And I was the meteor itself.

“Where do you think you’re going?”

With that quiet murmur, I became one with the spear and plunged downward. My target was its wing, which served as both foreleg and arm.

Blinded by pain for a moment, the creature had no way to stop the meteor.

Fwoosh! Shraaaaaak!

Scorching Yang Qi blazed like a miniature sun, slicing through hide and scales and burning the flesh beneath. The wing, more than ten meters from top to bottom, split in two along the path of the spearhead.[^7]

—Krrrk…!

It was probably the worst pain the creature had ever experienced. The red eye of a beast that had spent its entire life as a predator flew wide.

—Kraaaaaaaaaah!

I landed lightly on the ground and regarded it with a cold, steady gaze.

Its fifty-meter bulk writhed within the billowing cloud of dust.[^8]

“Does it hurt?”

—Kwak! Kraaaaaah!

“That little?”

Compared to what it had done three years ago, this was nothing.

A single flap of its wings had shattered entire bodies. Heads clutched in its claws had vanished without a trace. Those swallowed by its enormous maw hadn’t even left corpses behind.

That was when I first learned how much blood and how many organs the human body contained.

How brutally a person could die.

“You bastard. I wouldn’t be satisfied even if I chewed you to death.”

An eye for an eye. A tooth for a tooth.

It would die here today, by my hand. And it would die horribly—exactly as I had imagined countless times before.

“This is just the beginning. Quit whining and get up.”

Whoooosh.

The wind stirred by my swinging spear swept away the dust.

Covered in blood and dirt, the creature glared at me as it panted heavily.

—Krrrk.

Dozens of blades were embedded throughout its body, and blood poured from its open wounds like waterfalls.

Of the wings that symbolized the Wyvern, only one remained.

It was still enormous and imposing, but there was no longer any trace of the dignity befitting a dragonkin offshoot and a Named Monster.

—Grrrrr…

Its eye, brimming with resentment and killing intent, glared at me.

The emotions conveyed by that gaze were unlike anything I had ever known from a monster.

“Watch how you look at me, or I’ll pluck that eye out first.”

I tossed out the words and began walking toward it.

That was when it happened.

—Hu. man.

“……!”

A single word made me doubt my own ears.

My feet froze. The corner of my eye twitched involuntarily.

*What did I just hear?*

But I hadn’t misheard it. The creature’s maw shifted, and a clearer pronunciation emerged.

—Do. you. want. to. kill. me?

A monster was speaking.

That very *monster*.

A groan slipped through my parted lips.

“This is impossible…”

—It’s. dif.fer.ent. from. be.fore.

The instant it finished speaking, its red eye turned completely bloodred.

And then…

—Heal.

Sssssss.

Magical power began gathering around the creature.

* * *

Carus the One-Eyed.

That was the Black Wyvern’s name.

Before earning that name, he had survived countless crises. He had fought not only monsters, but humans as well.

He had fought hundreds of battles where victory meant claiming prey and defeat meant becoming prey.

That day in the past had been no different.

Not until one human took his eye.

*How dare he? How dare a human lower than a bug do this to me!*

Carus was furious. At the same time, he made a vow.

He would kill the human who had taken his eye. Even if he never found him, he would kill other humans again and again.

Then one day, after endless battle and slaughter, he realized that he had grown to an enormous size and gained tremendous strength.

*Why? Did fighting humans make me stronger?*

Before long, Carus understood. It wasn’t his battles with humans that had made him stronger, but devouring other monsters.

Each time he did, something inside his body grew more powerful.

*What did the humans call it again? Ah, right.*

Magic Gems.

Once he understood the source of his strength, Carus began hunting Magic Gems.

He devoured other monsters, and instead of feasting on human flesh, he studied the magic equipment they carried.

*So this is how those human bastards use Magic Gems.*

The more Magic Gems he absorbed, the higher his Intelligence rose and the stronger he became.

As a Wyvern, a lesser branch of the dragonkin, Carus had possessed remarkable Intelligence to begin with. At last, he set foot in an entirely new realm.

*Magic, huh? Should I learn it?*

Carus built a new nest in a nameless wasteland. He killed everything that might get in his way and immersed himself in the study of magic.

Then he noticed the humans invading his territory.

*I haven’t even finished digesting the Magic Gems I ate earlier…*

Knowing that he was still incomplete, Carus decided to be patient.

Even when several humans recklessly approached his nest, he tried to ignore them.

Until he caught *that bastard’s* scent.

*My eye! It’s the human who took my eye!*

Carus saw red and immediately raced across the wasteland.

Using one of the humans he had deliberately allowed to escape as a guide, he finally came face-to-face with that bastard.

*I’ll kill him! I’ll chew him up, bones and all!*

But that bastard was strong. Even Carus, who had absorbed hundreds of Magic Gems, was pushed back helplessly.

Yet he still had one card left to play.

—Heal.

Sssssss.

His wounds closed, and the bleeding stopped. He couldn’t completely restore his torn wing, but this was enough.

—I’ll. kill. you. hu.man.

Jin Taekyung, his face filled with shock, clenched his teeth.

Having already experienced Jin Taekyung’s speed firsthand, Carus cast another spell without hesitation.

—Sloooow!

A faint trace of dragon blood flowed through Carus’s veins.

Five Slow spells stacked atop one another and enveloped Jin Taekyung’s body.

—Kehahahaha!

Carus burst into laughter as he watched Jin Taekyung move as slowly as possible.

That was when Jin Taekyung spoke.

“One hundred points to Agility.”

—……?

Whoosh.

Carus blinked.

A spearhead wreathed in blue flames filled his enormous eye.

“What are you looking at, you fucking bastard?”
